learningObjectives: Explain the developmental sequence underlying neural tube formation.
Identify the principal cells, structures and signals involved in neural tube formation.
Connect neural tube formation to later cognition and behaviour.
Interpret clinical findings without treating development as deterministic.

anatomy.label: Neural plate
anatomy.detail: The neural plate thickens and lengthens along the embryo.
anatomy.clinical: Its geometry sets the starting conditions for closure.

anatomy.label: Hinge points
anatomy.short: Regions that bend the neural plate
anatomy.detail: Median and dorsolateral hinge points help elevate and converge the folds.
anatomy.clinical: Disrupted cell-shape change can impair closure even when cell numbers are normal.

anatomy.label: Neural folds
anatomy.short: Raised edges that approach one another
anatomy.detail: The folds elevate and fuse along the dorsal midline.
anatomy.clinical: Closure is a moving process, not a single simultaneous event.

anatomy.label: Neural crest
anatomy.short: Migratory cells leaving the closing tube
anatomy.detail: Neural crest cells generate much of the peripheral nervous system and other tissues.
anatomy.clinical: Neural crest disorders can affect multiple organ systems.

anatomy.label: Neural tube lumen
anatomy.detail: The enclosed cavity later contributes to the ventricular system and spinal central canal.
anatomy.clinical: Abnormal fluid dynamics can later interact with ventricular development.

interaction.title: Neural Tube Formation sequence
interaction.instruction: Select a component, then run the sequence to follow development over time.

stages.label: Bend
stages.text: Hinge points lift the neural folds.

stages.label: Separate
stages.text: Neural crest cells migrate away from the tube.

quizBank.question: The neural tube later forms the:
quizBank.explanation: The central nervous system develops from the neural tube.

quizBank.question: Neural crest cells contribute importantly to the:
quizBank.explanation: Neural crest derivatives include much of the peripheral nervous system.

quizBank.question: Why is folic acid recommended before conception?
quizBank.explanation: Closure occurs in the first weeks, often before pregnancy is recognised.

quizBank.question: Spina bifida reflects failed closure primarily in the:
quizBank.explanation: Spina bifida involves incomplete closure in the spinal region.

quizBank.question: Neurulation requires:
options: Coordinated cell-shape change and tissue folding
quizBank.explanation: Mechanical and molecular processes jointly drive folding and fusion.
